name: The Dharma Centre of Canada

location.address: 1267 Galway Road, RR 1, Kinmount, Ontario K0M 2A0, Canada

tradition: Non-sectarian Buddhist meditation centre (Theravada Insight, Zen, and Tibetan Vajrayana) in the tradition of founder Namgyal Rinpoche
technique: Varies by visiting teacher and retreat - includes Insight/mindfulness meditation, Zen sesshin-style sitting, and Tibetan Vajrayana practices such as Dream Yoga and the Six Yogas of Naropa; the Solo Retreat program supports self-guided practice developed with a personal or Core Teacher.
teacherAccess: Group retreats are led by visiting Core and guest Teachers with Dharma talks, group practice and interview opportunities; Solo Retreat participants have periodic guidance from a Core Teacher as set out in a signed agreement for their stay.
retreatOptions: Group retreats of a weekend to about a week led by visiting teachers across traditions (Zen sesshin, Tibetan Vajrayana, Insight-rooted silent retreats and workshops); a year-round Solo Retreat program for experienced meditators, from two nights up to a month or longer; online programs.
about: The Dharma Centre of Canada is one of the oldest meditation centres in North America, founded in Toronto in 1966 by the Venerable Ananda Bodhi - later enthroned as Karma Tenzin Dorje Namgyal Rinpoche in the Karma Kagyu lineage - who had first trained in Theravada Insight meditation in Burma, Thailand and Sri Lanka before re-ordaining as a Tibetan Buddhist teacher. Its 400-acre forested property near Kinmount, in the Kawartha Highlands about two hours northeast of Toronto, holds a Tibetan stupa, a Burmese pagoda and a Sri Lankan dagoba built by students of the different traditions the founder studied under, reflecting the centre's non-sectarian, cross-lineage approach to Buddhist practice. Visiting teachers lead group retreats of varying lengths and traditions throughout the year - including Zen sesshin, Tibetan Vajrayana practice and Insight-rooted silent retreats - while the centre's Solo Retreat program lets experienced meditators book a private cabin for self-guided practice ranging from a weekend up to a year or more, supported by periodic guidance from the Core Teachers. Retreatants stay in simple single rooms or off-grid cabins across roughly 100 developed acres, take three home-cooked meals a day, contribute up to an hour of daily 'generosity yoga' (volunteer work), and are asked to keep the Five (or optionally Eight) Precepts for the duration of their stay.
schedule: Varies by retreat and teacher; solo retreatants follow a practice structure set out in a Memorandum of Understanding with a Core Teacher, including a daily one-hour work-as-practice period ("generosity yoga") and, for longer stays, periodic check-ins to review progress.
cost: Group retreats charge a course fee (amount set per retreat) that covers room and board; a separate voluntary dana offering is customary for the visiting teacher, with the suggested guideline being roughly what one would pay per hour for one's own work.
foodNotes: Three whole-food, home-made meals a day are included in the course fee, with meat or fish served every other day; vegetarian and gluten-free diets can be accommodated with advance notice.
workNotes: Retreatants are expected to contribute up to one hour of daily volunteer work ('generosity yoga'), typically clean-up after meals or common-area tidying, to help keep retreat fees down.
